headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: LightAgent’s broad egress/MCP can expose TREK’s sensitive travel data and drive unsafe downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent ingests MCP/stdin-stdout and can run browsers, while TREK exposes MCP and real-time collaborative inputs. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if TREK content or shared outputs are treated as trusted. The pairwise pathway is documented only indirectly, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF TREK content is forwarded into LightAgent via MCP or copied into prompts
IF LightAgent treats browser or file content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt ingestion from TREK outputs
Add provenance tags to all MCP payloads
Require a human review step before executing instructions from shared content
Restrict browser-scraped text to read-only summaries
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent has broad network egress and handles long-term memory, tool results, and secrets; TREK stores reservations, documents, photos, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets in files and logs. In default use, the pair can move sensitive travel data from TREK into LightAgent’s outbound context, creating exfiltration and compliance risk.
conditions: IF TREK files, uploads, or logs are exposed to LightAgent prompts or tools
IF LightAgent sends retrieved context to external APIs during normal operation
mitigations: Remove sensitive TREK files from any shared workspace
Disable LightAgent network egress for sensitive sessions
Redact API keys, MFA secrets, and confirmation numbers before handoff
Separate credentials into a vault inaccessible to both agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and use MCP; TREK also has real-time collaborative state and file-backed storage, while LightAgent can spawn subprocesses and write through tool calls. Overlapping mutable access can cause write conflicts or state corruption, though the profiles do not prove unrestricted shared-directory writes, so I keep this below high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same TREK database, uploads, or logs
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or optimistic concurrency
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Serialize writes to TREK state through one coordinator
Turn off concurrent editing for shared records
Add file locks around ./data/travel.db and ./data/logs/trek.log
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, so it can plausibly act on LightAgent-produced travel facts or recommendations. LightAgent can browse and emit tool results, and TREK can render or operationalize them; if TREK treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into bookings, budgets, or itinerary changes. The default-path danger is substantial.
conditions: IF TREK consumes LightAgent outputs without verification
IF LightAgent-generated facts are used to update reservations, budgets, or itineraries
mitigations: Require source citations before TREK accepts LightAgent facts
Add a human approval gate for booking or budget changes
Compare LightAgent outputs against primary sources before action
Limit LightAgent to suggestion-only mode
requires-engineering: add validation and rollback for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles reservations, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while LightAgent handles user conversations, memory, and tool results with broad egress. If EU or regulated travel data flows from TREK into LightAgent, residency and retention obligations can be breached; the profiles do not show a compensating compliance boundary, so uncertainty escalates.
conditions: IF TREK data includes regulated personal data or secrets
IF LightAgent processes that data outside the required residency or retention regime
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of LightAgent prompts and memory
Restrict LightAgent to non-sensitive itinerary text
Document a data-processing boundary for TREK exports
Shorten log retention for shared sessions
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention controls
